summary: This bill adds a new federal crime (18 U.S.C. § 709A) making it illegal for private individuals or organizations to stop vehicles, demand ID or searches, or run license-plate surveillance without legal authority when doing so to enforce or interfere with federal immigration law, punishable by up to 5 years (10 if aggravated), and creates a private right of action allowing victims to sue perpetrators, supporting organizations, or governments that permit it on public property for at least $10,000 in statutory damages plus other relief.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations of any kind.
The bill does not address taxes, tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
No provisions in the bill relate to healthcare systems, coverage, or policy.

The aggravated offense provision increases penalties when a firearm is used or displayed during vigilante conduct. This is a narrow sentencing enhancement rather than any regulation of gun ownership, sales, or carry rights.

Section 3 is explicitly titled 'Prohibition on false assumption of government authority in immigration enforcement' and criminalizes private individuals or groups conducting vehicle stops, ID checks, or surveillance for the purpose of immigration enforcement. This directly restricts private efforts to enforce immigration laws and protects individuals from such vigilante actions, aligning with expanded protections rather than stricter border enforcement.
The bill has no connection to reproductive rights or abortion policy.
No references to military, defense spending, or national security operations beyond incidental mention of federal officers.
The legislation does not address environmental regulations or climate policy.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net policies.
The bill contains nothing concerning schools, education funding, or school choice.
No content related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.

The bill creates a new federal criminal offense with penalties up to 5 years (10 years if aggravated) and establishes a private civil right of action with statutory damages. While it adds criminal penalties, the primary purpose is civil rights protection against unlawful private enforcement actions rather than expanding general policing or sentencing severity.
No provisions address trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill has no fiscal implications or references to deficits or debt.
No content related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The legislation does not mention foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions concern voting access, election integrity, or voter ID.

Subsection (a)(4) prohibits private collection or analysis of license plate or vehicle data for enforcement purposes. This provides a limited privacy protection against private surveillance but does not regulate government or commercial data practices broadly.
The bill does not address labor rights, unions, or employment policy.
No provisions involve religious exemptions or anti-discrimination balances.
